answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may vote or earn rewards. A single operator creating a spiral of sybils must lock more tokens for every identity, tying up capital and risking slashing if those accounts coordinate in a prohibited way. The rule does not prove identities are unique; it makes influence costly, so an attacker must commit real resources rather than minting names as cheaply as a pearl or falcon badge.
